standard_prerequisites.name: Reflexive sheaves over a regular scheme of dimension two on a nonempty open where a coherent sheaf is locally free of rank r have invertible determinant, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the two determinants invertible, so that the canonical map between them can be compared as a section of an invertible sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The structure theorem for finite modules over a discrete valuation ring (or over a PID), cited from the more-algebra chapter, and the fact that dividing a finite module by its torsion does not change its double dual
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 3312-3315 and used at 3316-3322
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the algebraic problem to free modules of rank r, where the determinant is available.

standard_prerequisites.name: The vanishing order of the determinant of a map between free modules equals the length of the cokernel, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the exact vanishing order s of the determinant in the reduced case, which is at most the minimum of s and r.

core_obligations: Invertibility and the canonical map: assumption (1) plus the same-chapter result on reflexive sheaves over a regular surface makes the two determinants invertible, taking r-th exterior powers and double duals is functorial so there is a canonical map between them which is an isomorphism over the nonempty open of (1) and hence nonzero, and the claim reduces to showing that this map, viewed as a section of the difference of the two determinants, vanishes at no codimension point except the generic point of D, and there with order at most the minimum of s and r (proof lines 3297-3308).

Algebraic translation: over the discrete valuation ring A at the generic point of D with fraction field K, set up an exact sequence M to M' to N to 0 of finite A-modules with the two generic ranks equal to r and with N isomorphic to s copies of the residue field, and state the target: the induced map between the double duals of the r-th exterior powers vanishes to order at most the minimum of s and r (proof lines 3309-3316).

Torsion reduction: dividing a finite module by its torsion submodule does not change the double dual, so replace M and M' by their torsion-free quotients, observe that the map becomes injective and the torsion of M' injects into N, and therefore reduce to the case where M and M' are free of rank r and N is s copies of the residue field (proof lines 3316-3327).

Reduced case: with M and M' free of rank r the canonical map is the determinant of the map between them, whose vanishing order is s by the cited algebra lemma, and since N has s generators the bound by the minimum of s and r follows (proof lines 3327-3331).
proof_roadmap: Use functoriality of the determinant to turn the problem into the vanishing order of one section of an invertible sheaf at the generic point of the divisor (proof lines 3297-3308).

Translate to a discrete valuation ring, discard torsion without changing double duals, and compute the vanishing order as the determinant of a map between free modules of rank r (proof lines 3309-3331).
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the twist relating the determinants of the two middle terms of an exact sequence F to F' to the pushforward of a rank s bundle on an effective Cartier divisor of a regular surface: the two double duals of the r-th exterior powers are invertible and differ by a twist by k times the divisor with k between 0 and the minimum of s and r (statement lines 3276-3295). The counted proof has two layers: geometrically it uses functoriality of taking exterior powers and double duals to produce a canonical nonzero map and reduces the claim to a vanishing-order statement for a section of an invertible sheaf at the generic point of the divisor (proof lines 3297-3308); algebraically it translates that to the discrete valuation ring at that generic point and disposes of torsion, which does not change double duals, to reduce to free modules of rank r where the map becomes a determinant whose vanishing order is the length of the cokernel (proof lines 3309-3331). It is H2: the reductions are carried out in the counted span, and the deep input is the cited algebra statement on vanishing orders of determinants.
